paper.title: Efficient Automatic CASH via Rising Bandits

parameters.restriction: each arm has a fixed deterministic reward function r_k(n) of its pull count, bounded in [0,1], increasing and concave (Assumption 1)

unmapped: Rested rising bandit: reward of arm k on its n-th pull is r_k(n), deterministic, increasing and concave in n
Objective is the maximum observed reward J(T;pi)=max_t r_{pi(t)}(N_{pi(t)}(t)+1); regret is max over policies of J minus J of the learner (not cumulative regret)
settings.definition_quote: In Rising Bandits, we model the non-stationary reward sequences of the arms as follows: each arm $k$ has a fixed underlying reward function denoted by $r_k(.)$. All the reward functions are bounded within $[0, 1]$. When the agent pulls arm $k$ for the $n^{th}$ time, he receives an instantaneous reward $r_k(n)$. ... the objective of the agent in CASH is to maximize the observed reward within $T$ ... \textbf{Assumption 1. } (Rising) $\forall{k} \in [K]$, $r_k(n)$ is bounded, increasing, and concave in $n$.

symbols.r_opt: reward function r_{k*}(.) of the optimal arm for horizon T
symbols.gamma_id: gamma(T) = max_k gamma_k(T), the number of steps needed to distinguish suboptimal arm k from the optimal arm via the upper/lower bound elimination criterion
symbols.n_paper: the paper's n (not defined in the theorem; presumably the number of arms K)

conditions: Assumption 1: each r_k is bounded in [0,1], increasing and concave

source.quote: Suppose Assumption 1 holds. The proposed algorithm achieves regret bounded by, R(T; \bar{\pi}) \le r_{k_{\ast}^T}(T) - r_{k_{\ast}^T}(T - (n-1)\gamma(T)).

results.notes: Regret is with respect to the max-observed-reward objective, not cumulative reward; quantity set to 'other'. Rewards are deterministic so the bound holds surely. Meaning of n in the theorem is not defined in the main text (likely K).

symbols.r_opt: reward function value r_{k*}(T) of the optimal arm
symbols.r_uni: max_k r_k(T/K), the best reward reached by the uniform policy pulling each arm T/K times

source.quote: When the problem-dependent term $\gamma(T)$ satisfies: $\gamma(T) \le \frac{KT - T}{K(K-1)}$, the regret of the proposed algorithm will not be worse than the average strategy's. R(T; \bar{\pi}) \le R(T; \pi_{uni}).

results.notes: Comparison with the average policy; expression substitutes the paper's stated regret of the uniform policy.
